# Actuation Principles {.unnumbered}

Part III investigates the input/output subsystem and peripheral boundaries of the Stochastic Computer. When a neural model commands tools, stochastic tokens must interface with deterministic software environments. We develop typed tool application binary interfaces (Model Context Protocol), analyze the physical breakdown of the $W \oplus X$ execution boundary in neural reasoning, and engineer hardware-virtualized sandboxes (Firecracker microVMs, WebAssembly, and Copy-on-Write filesystems) to enforce zero-trust isolation.

::: {#pri-vol3-strict-action-abi .callout-principle title="The typed action contract"}

**Invariant**: Stochastic models must interface with deterministic environments through typed, schema-validated, versioned, and idempotent protocol contracts.

**Implication**: Free-form text parsing must be replaced with typed protocol standards (Model Context Protocol) and grammar-constrained logit decoding at the hardware peripheral transceiver.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-zero-trust-sandboxing .callout-principle title="Zero-trust virtualization and defense-in-depth"}

**Invariant**: Because neural models interleave prompt instructions and untrusted data within the same token stream ($W \oplus X$ breakdown), runtimes must assume model compromise and isolate all tool execution inside ephemeral hardware boundaries.

**Implication**: Tool execution must occur inside hardware-isolated microVMs with strict network egress firewalls and Copy-on-Write snapshots to prevent data exfiltration and persistent host corruption.

:::
